an3.21:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
an3.21:1.3: Then the Venerable Saviṭṭha and the Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita approached the Venerable Sāriputta and exchanged greetings with him.
an3.21:1.4: When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, they sat down to one side. The Venerable Sāriputta then said to the Venerable Saviṭṭha:
an3.21:2.1: “Friend Saviṭṭha, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world.
an3.21:2.3: The body witness, the one attained to view, and the one liberated by faith.
an3.21:2.4: These are the three kinds of persons found existing in the world.
an3.21:2.5: Which of these three kinds of persons do you consider the most excellent and sublime?”
an3.21:3.5: of those three kinds of persons, I consider the one liberated by faith to be the most excellent and sublime.
an3.21:3.7: Because this person’s faculty of faith is predominant.”
an3.21:4.1: Then the Venerable Sāriputta said to the Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita:
an3.21:4.2: “Friend Koṭṭhita, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world….
an3.21:4.6: Which of these three kinds of persons do you consider the most excellent and sublime?”
an3.21:5.5: of those three kinds of persons, I consider the body witness to be the most excellent and sublime.
an3.21:5.7: Because this person’s faculty of concentration is predominant.”
an3.21:6.1: Then the Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita said to the Venerable Sāriputta:
an3.21:6.2: “Friend Sāriputta, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world….
an3.21:6.6: Which of these three kinds of persons do you consider the most excellent and sublime?”
an3.21:7.4: “Friend Koṭṭhita, of those three kinds of persons,
an3.21:7.5: I consider the one attained to view to be the most excellent and sublime.
an3.21:7.7: Because this person’s faculty of wisdom is predominant.”
an3.21:8.1: Then the Venerable Sāriputta said to the Venerable Saviṭṭha and the Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita:
an3.21:8.2: “Friends, we have each explained according to our own ideal.
an3.21:8.3: Come, let’s approach the Blessed One and report this matter to him.
an3.21:8.4: We will retain it in mind as he explains it to us.”
an3.21:8.5: “Yes, friend,” the Venerable Saviṭṭha and the Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita replied.
an3.21:8.6: Then the Venerable Sāriputta, the Venerable Saviṭṭha, and the Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side.
an3.21:8.7: The Venerable Sāriputta then reported to him the entire conversation that had taken place. The Blessed One said:
an3.21:9.1: “It isn’t easy, Sāriputta, to make a definitive declaration about this matter and say:
an3.21:9.2: ‘Of these three kinds of persons, this one is the most excellent and sublime.’
an3.21:9.3: (1) “For it is possible that a person liberated by faith is practicing for arahantship, while a body witness and one attained to view are once-returners or non-returners.
an3.21:10.1: It isn’t easy, Sāriputta, to make a definitive declaration about this matter and say:
an3.21:10.2: ‘Of these three kinds of persons, this one is the most excellent and sublime.’
an3.21:10.3: (2) “It is possible that a person who is a body witness is practicing for arahantship, while one liberated by faith and one attained to view are once-returners or non-returners.
an3.21:11.1: It isn’t easy, Sāriputta, to make a definitive declaration about this matter and say:
an3.21:11.2: ‘Of these three kinds of persons, this one is the most excellent and sublime.’
an3.21:11.3: (3) “It is possible that a person attained to view is practicing for arahantship, while one liberated by faith and a body witness are once-returners or non-returners.
an3.21:12.1: It isn’t easy, Sāriputta, to make a definitive declaration about this matter and say:
an3.21:12.2: ‘Of these three kinds of persons, this one is the most excellent and sublime.’”
